answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to solve a sequential memory-hard puzzle seeded from its prior attestation hash. The challenge forces filling a large walnut-sized RAM buffer with a dune-specific chain of dependencies before the final fable of the proof can be emitted. Attackers incur full sequential time and memory cost per fake identity; parallel hardware yields no speedup because steps depend on prior state, making mass Sybil farms economically prohibitive compared to honest single agents.
